osaka_kinryu_ramen_dotonbori.notes: [Ramen · the 24-hour bowl under Dotonbori's giant dragon] Minami's famous all-night ramen stand, known for the huge dragon sculpture over the shop. There are only two choices, ramen (¥900 in October 2026, after a ¥200 rise) or chashu ramen, in a tonkotsu the listing describes as rich, made from pork bones and chicken feet with a secret tare. Most 2026 diners found it surprisingly light, with medium-thin, slightly curly noodles. The fun is the free kimchi, garlic and garlic chives to load in. Take a number and carry your bowl from the counter to tatami or counter seats. Queues are mostly overseas visitors late at night but move fast. Opinions vary: a nostalgic finish to a night out for many, lukewarm and thin for one critic.

osaka_kamukura_dotonbori.notes: [Ramen · Kamukura's light cabbage ramen on its home street] The Dotonbori shop of Kamukura, now a nationwide chain that long-time fans still call a local treasure, with 71 seats and open from 10:00 to 08:00 the next morning. The signature "delicious ramen" (¥850 in October 2026) is a light, gently sweet, secret-recipe broth heaped with crunchy napa cabbage and thin-sliced pork. The most popular version adds small chashu and a soft-boiled egg (¥1,270); there's kara-age (¥430), gyoza and seasonal bowls such as a hot-and-sour soup with Zhenjiang vinegar and cilantro. Order on the table tablet. It's easy to eat and veg-heavy, though one diner found it too salty, and the noodles are soft, almost udon-like.

osaka_kinkuemon_dotonbori.notes: [Ramen · Osaka Black, the jet-black shoyu, through the night] Since 2011 the Dotonbori branch of Kinkuemon, a shop famous for sharp shoyu ramen, set just off the main strip by the Kinryū queue. It has 41 seats over two floors and is open through the night (24 hours Friday to Sunday). The signature Osaka Black is a glossy jet-black soy broth with chicken stock and a seafood edge, buttery chicken-fat aroma and a faintly bitter soy finish. Choose thin noodles (most recommend them) or thick, topped with chashu, menma, green onion and a soft egg; extra noodles are extra. Also on the menu: Red Shoyu, King Shoyu, and Osaka Kinjou Shoyu, a clear chicken-and-light-soy broth that one 34-visit regular likes at 8 am. Buy a ticket at the machine outside; garlic on request. ¥1,000–1,200 a bowl; a few found it pricey for tourists or the service curt.

osaka_hayashida_dotonbori.notes: [Ramen · Tokyo's Hayashida right under the Glico sign] The first Kansai branch, opened in 2022, of Ramen Hayashida, a Shinjuku shop famous for queues and run by INGS Co. It's a 16-seat counter one floor below the Glico running man, southwest of Ebisubashi. The signature is a clear shoyu broth of duck and Daisen-dori chicken (¥900; the special with a "Maximum Koitama" egg ¥1,200) on firm, thin whole-wheat noodles, with pork-shoulder and chicken-breast chashu. There's also a creamy chicken paitan, a refined tsukemen (special ¥1,250), mazesoba with truffle-sauce egg, and summer yuzu cold ramen (¥950) with yuzu jelly. Add a TKG or oyakodon (¥350–400). Buy tickets at the entrance machine. Light and quick, with friendly staff: a handy fast lunch when Minami's big names are queuing.

osaka_zundoya_dotonbori.notes: [Ramen · Himeji back-fat tonkotsu, round the clock] The Dotonbori branch, opened 31 October 2025, of Zundōya, a Himeji-founded chain with over a hundred shops (about 106 in Japan and 4 in Shanghai, per a December 2025 visitor). It sits just east of Ebisubashi and is open 24 hours. The broth is pork bone with a slightly creamy soy seasoning and as much back fat as you choose (light, regular, rich or extra rich). Noodles are house-made: ultra-thin straight (recommended) or curly. The motomi (original) ramen is ¥860, ajitama ¥980, and all-toppings up to ¥1,360; summer brought a cold ramen with grated daikon. Season at the table with pepper, pickled ginger, garlic, chili oil, sesame and takana. Buy a ticket outside (transit IC accepted) and head upstairs. A Kansai-friendly tonkotsu with a hint of sweetness.

osaka_ichiran_namba_midosuji.notes: [Ramen · Ichiran's pork-free "no tonkotsu" shop] The one Ichiran operating under its "100% no tonkotsu used" concept: the familiar experience (booth counters with partitions, an order sheet, Arita-ware bowls) but a broth developed from beef bones and chicken, so people who can't eat pork can have Ichiran. Diners call it surprisingly rich and creamy, very like tonkotsu, with the signature red secret sauce. One found it lacked real tonkotsu's punch. Instead of pork chashu there's sweet-spicy seasoned beef (gyūyarō), plus soft salted egg, extra garlic and a matcha pudding. The 100% pork-free ramen was ¥1,280 in July 2026. Expect 30–80-minute waits (scan a QR code and return); a 9 am weekday arrival walked straight in. 25 seats, many overseas visitors.

osaka_kinryu_ramen_midosuji.notes: [Ramen · Kinryū's standing yatai on Midōsuji] One of Kinryū's several Namba shops, under a big dragon sign on Midōsuji. It's done in a food-stall style: buy a ticket, then mostly stand at the counter or use the tables by the pavement, with the kitchen in full view. Like the Dotonbori shop, it serves a simple tonkotsu ramen (¥900) that most find lighter than its strong pork aroma suggests, plus free kimchi, garlic and garlic chives to pile on. A seven-time visitor praises the old-school simplicity of a shop that has served for over 35 years; a first-timer was underwhelmed. Turnover is quick and it's open 24 hours, handy at 2 am. Fans call it Osaka soul food from before the chain went national: a light, slightly sweet, almost Western-style broth loaded with napa cabbage, the kind people want after drinking instead of heavy tonkotsu. One diner insists it tastes different from other branches. Try the vegetable ramen (¥1,110) or the ramen, kara-age and rice set (about ¥1,350); summer brought a cold pork-shabu ramen with ume, shiso and grated daikon (¥1,250). Buy a ticket at the machine out front. Service can be flat late at night, and one summer visitor found the cabbage bitter.

osaka_makotoya_shinsaibashi.notes: [Ramen · beef-bone white soup, all night] An 18-seat counter, since 2011, three doors east of Mitsudera, serving Makotoya's beef-bone "gyū-paitan" around the clock. Regulars go when they want something that isn't miso, shoyu or shio. The beef broth is rich and smooth but not heavy, with a beefy aroma and sweetness that clings to thin noodles (choose your firmness). The favourite is the spicy red version with soft-boiled egg, chashu, wood ear, bean sprouts and green onion in a red bowl. Doctor it at the table with fresh garlic, garlic chips, pickled ginger and white sesame. Morioka cold noodles were ¥1,010 in August 2026. Buy a ticket at the machine by the door; one visitor found the street queue was for the malatang shop nearby.

chef_bio.background: Shinsaibashi branch of Makotoya (Tabelog listing name).

anecdotes.text: "Their beef bone ramen has a unique flavor profile, with noodles that carry the aroma and sweetness of beef… I ordered my favorite, the spicy red beef bone white soup ramen, paired with fried rice." — September 2026.
"The ramen features a rich and smooth broth that truly captures the essence of beef bones. It's flavorful without being too heavy, and the thin noodles pair perfectly with it." — August 2026.

osaka_matsusakagyu_yakiniku_m_hozenji_ha.gf_detail: The restaurant tells FindMeGlutenFree that every food item can be made gluten-free on request, but asks for notice when you book: "Advance reservation required for gluten-free dining." It makes its own gluten-free sauces, including soy sauce and ponzu. Celiac reviewers on FMGF (14 recent ratings) describe staff who confirm gluten-free at the table, swap single items in a set and change the grill between gluten-free and regular dishes. One 2025 diner was brought regular sauces by a different server and caught it by asking. It is not a gluten-free kitchen. Say you are celiac when you book and again when you sit down.
osaka_matsusakagyu_yakiniku_m_hozenji_ha.vegan_detail: A Matsusaka-beef yakiniku house. Replying on FMGF, the manager says it also offers vegan menu options, but no vegan dish is described anywhere. Ask when booking.
osaka_matsusakagyu_yakiniku_m_hozenji_ha.hours_raw: Weekdays 12:00–15:00 (L.O. 14:30) and 17:00–23:00 (L.O. 22:30); weekends and holidays 12:00–23:00; no fixed holiday (official page, hours from 21 June 2026). Book ahead; gluten-free needs advance notice.
osaka_matsusakagyu_yakiniku_m_hozenji_ha.notes: [Yakiniku · gluten-free Matsusaka beef by Hōzenji] The "hanare" annex of Yakiniku M's Hōzenji branch: a second-floor room off Hōzenji Yokochō where you take your shoes off at the door, with seven tables, six of them semi-private and one a private room. Matsusaka beef is grilled at the table. It is a celiac favourite: the restaurant says any dish can be made gluten-free with notice, and it makes its own gluten-free soy sauce, ponzu and dipping sauces, so the marinated beef and garlic rice can be done too. Celiac reviewers rave about the staff ("Best GF meal we've had in Japan"). It is pricey: one diner put it at ¥8,800–12,000 a head, another had the ¥12,000 premium course. When it was full, staff walked guests to another branch nearby. Book and mention gluten-free when you do.

chef_bio.background: Part of the Matsusakagyu Yakiniku M group of Osaka yakiniku restaurants (official site); one FMGF reviewer counted four locations.

osaka_genji_soba_hozenji_sando.gf_detail: The soba is hand-made from 100% buckwheat (juwari). The menu marks gluten-free dishes, and celiac reviewers on FindMeGlutenFree (101 recent ratings) describe a separate, celiac-labelled section. On the official menu, the tempura is made with buckwheat and rice flour and "Fried in a Dedicated Gluten-Free Fryer". Gluten-free dipping sauce and soy sauce are made for gluten-free orders, while the regular sauces are also in use, so ask. FMGF flags that it is NOT a dedicated gluten-free facility. Several reviewers say the celiac-safe tempura and menu are dinner only. Staff ask whether you are celiac. Tell them, and reserve the set courses ahead.
osaka_genji_soba_hozenji_sando.vegan_detail: The set courses note: "Gluten-Free & Vegan options are available upon advance request." There is a vegan soba on the à la carte menu, but in September 2026 a reviewer was asked whether egg was OK after ordering it, so it may only be vegetarian. Ask about the dashi and egg.
osaka_genji_soba_hozenji_sando.hours_raw: 11:30–21:30 (L.O. 21:30), break 14:30–17:00; closed some Wednesdays (水曜不定休) (official site). Lunch and dinner set courses by reservation, upstairs. Reviewers say the celiac-safe tempura is dinner only. The original shop at Namba 4-5-8 is closed for now; this Hōzenji Sandō shop opened in March 2026.
osaka_genji_soba_hozenji_sando.notes: [Soba · 100% buckwheat and gluten-free tempura on Hōzenji Sandō] A soba house founded in 1929 that moved in March 2026 into a new shop on the stone-paved Hōzenji approach; the old shop is closed for now. The noodles are hand-made from 100% buckwheat (you can watch them being cut in the front window), which makes it a celiac favourite. The menu marks gluten-free and celiac-safe dishes, and the prawn and vegetable tempura is made with buckwheat and rice flour in a dedicated gluten-free fryer. The classic order is cold zaru soba with a big wild prawn and vegetable tempura (¥2,950). There are also grated-daikon, yam and Tamba black-bean natto soba, beef and duck soba, a two-soba lunch (¥1,850), and set courses upstairs by reservation. Some find the broth fishy. You order by QR code at the table, and dinner waits can stretch at busy times.

osaka_naki_vegan_sweets.hours_raw: Not listed on the official site. An FMGF reviewer (August 2026) found it open 13:00–20:00. Check before going. About four seats; takeaway available; also sells online.
osaka_naki_vegan_sweets.notes: [Sweets · vegan and gluten-free tarts off Dotonbori] A tiny, quiet cake shop on a Namba side street with about four seats. Everything is vegan and gluten-free, and it is a celiac favourite (FMGF marks it reported dedicated gluten-free). Expect small tarts and cakes, around ¥1,000 each: mango, mixed berry cheesecake, chocolate pistachio, matcha and white chocolate, strawberry chocolate. Reviewers single out the cashew cream on a coarse almond crust, and the rice-flour and coconut-oil cookies, which one family bought to take home after being given some free. There is Italian espresso and peach cream soda. Service is gentle, once by a host in a kimono, though one 2026 diner found it unfriendly. Takeaway, and an online shop.

osaka_vim_gf_vegan_okonomiyaki.gf_detail: A gluten-free okonomiyaki restaurant. FindMeGlutenFree marks it "Reported to be dedicated gluten-free", and celiac reviewers (through October 2026) call it entirely gluten-free and safe for coeliacs, with Kirin gluten-free and organic gluten-free beer. Reported features include a dedicated gluten-free fryer and kitchen. The restaurant itself publishes nothing beyond its name, so this rests on community reports. Confirm when you book.
osaka_vim_gf_vegan_okonomiyaki.vegan_detail: Despite "Vegan" in its name, the menu also has meat and seafood: reviewers ate pork-belly okonomiyaki, grilled scallops, fried chicken and pork noodles. The vegan options include battered tofu and rice balls ("some vegan options"). Ask whether the batter, sauce and dashi for the vegan dishes are plant-based.
osaka_vim_gf_vegan_okonomiyaki.hours_raw: No hours published. Reviewers: opens at 17:00 (June 2026); closed Thursdays (April 2026); once closed an hour early (October 2026). About six seats. Reservation strongly advised (booking online needs a Japanese phone number); queue before opening otherwise. No children under 18 (FMGF tip, June 2026). One meal and one drink per person (May 2026).
osaka_vim_gf_vegan_okonomiyaki.notes: [Okonomiyaki · gluten-free okonomiyaki off Dotonbori] A tiny gluten-free okonomiyaki spot up a narrow alley off Dotonbori, with a counter downstairs and one table upstairs (about six seats). For celiac travellers it is a rare safe way to eat Osaka's signature dish. Reviewers order pork-belly okonomiyaki, stir-fried noodles and pasta, oyster mushrooms, tempura, battered tofu with rice balls, grilled scallops and fried chicken, with a Kirin gluten-free beer. The name says vegan, but meat and seafood are on the menu, so ask. Book ahead (online booking needs a Japanese phone number) or queue before the 5 pm opening. Several were turned away. Portions are small and prices high, one meal and one drink per person is expected, under-18s are not admitted, and it is reported closed on Thursdays. One reviewer mentions a sister restaurant around the corner.

osaka_ichiran_dotonbori_bekkan.hours_raw: Flavour-concentration counter open 24 hours; table seats 8:00–23:00 (official page, which warns seats and hours can change at short notice). Open year-round (Tabelog). Buy a ticket and fill in the order sheet while you queue.
osaka_ichiran_dotonbori_bekkan.notes: [Ramen · Ichiran's big Dotonbori annex, open all night] Ichiran's 82-seat annex at the Sennichimae end of Dotonbori, since 2015. The 30-seat booth counter runs 24 hours, and the table floors run 8:00–23:00. It is the familiar ritual: buy a ticket while you queue, then tick richness, fat, garlic, green or white onion, the red secret sauce and noodle firmness on the order sheet. The bowl is Hakata-style tonkotsu with firm, very thin noodles. One diner found it light and not greasy, another rich with no off-odour. The natural tonkotsu ramen was ¥1,180 and extra noodles ¥210 (August 2026), with a soft salted egg at ¥160. Queues can reach an hour (October 2026), even 10 minutes at 2 am. The table floors suit groups and families: one August visitor noted an adult can bring up to five children free. Souvenirs are sold on the way out.

chef_bio.background: Ichiran chain (ichiran.com), which calls itself a company that researches tonkotsu ramen more than anyone in the world and serves only tonkotsu ramen.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「とんこつラーメンを世界一研究する会社」 (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Natural tonkotsu ramen with the red secret sauce.

osaka_sakunosaku_sennichimae.notes: [Ramen · the old-school Naniwa tonkotsu counter on Sennichimae] A long-running 11-seat L-shaped counter on the Sennichimae shopping street under a "Ganso Naniwa Tonkotsu" sign, open from 5 am to late, and round the clock at weekends. Its Osaka-style tonkotsu is light and slightly sweet, with thin straight noodles, chashu, naruto, menma and green onion (¥1,080; ¥1,250 with a scalp-tingling spicy miso), and the first kaedama is free. Season it with the pickled ginger, sesame and garlic on the counter. The mountainous chashu ramen is ¥2,200. Several diners say the ¥100 gyoza with a ramen beat the ramen itself. Summer brings a chilled yuzu-lemon shio ramen with ginger (¥1,380), and there's a shrimp-miso abura-soba and tantan tsukemen. Some find it pricey for what it is. Buy a ticket out front. Smoking is allowed.

The signature torokotsu ramen comes with two big pieces of tender pork, nori, menma, naruto and green onion. Free kimchi on the counter cuts the richness. Newer additions include garlic tonkotsu ramen (April 2026) and champon, and the fried rice has a following. Regulars say the old queues have eased, the crowd is now largely overseas visitors, and the regular bowl tastes lighter than before. The restroom is up narrow stairs.

The draw is a frothy beef-bone and chicken white soup: rich and creamy but easy to finish, built on chicken carcass and beef knuckle with a soy kaeshi and back-fat finish over thin straight noodles. It comes with two chashu, one charred and one tender, plus a runny seasoned egg, menma and green onion. There's also a lighter tonkotsu and a mala-style chili condiment on the table. Prices are high: a limited bowl topped ¥2,000 in September 2026, and the strip-loin rice bowl in the set ran salty. One diner flagged cleanliness. Cards and electronic payment accepted.

osaka_matsusakagyu_yakiniku_m_sennichima.notes: [Yakiniku · gluten-free Matsusaka beef off Sennichimae] The Dotonbori-Sennichimae branch of Yakiniku M, on the second floor of a building just off the Sennichimae shopping street, about 100 m east of its Hōzenji Yokochō sister. It is larger than its sisters: 14 tables, seven of them in private rooms, curtained semi-private seating, a hall for groups of up to 32, a lift, and wheelchair access to the table. Matsusaka-beef courses are grilled at the table. For celiac diners the draw is the sauces, which the general manager says are all gluten-free. Staff even bring out the labelled soy sauce bottle, and one server who is celiac comes up again and again in reviews. Reviewers had non-GF set-course items swapped, though one notes the soup is the exception. Dinner daily, plus weekend lunch.

osaka_abeno_hub_namba.notes: [Okonomiyaki · gluten-free rice-flour okonomiyaki near the Glico sign] A casual bar-restaurant about five minutes from the Glico running man, with what it calls British roots: organic wine, European-style chūhai and British organic tea alongside beer and whisky. The gyoza are wheat and share the griddle, so skip them. Usually there's no queue when nearby okonomiyaki places have long lines. The chef-owner speaks good English, and ordering is by app. Smoking only on the outside terrace.

osaka_oko_fun_okonomiyaki_bar.notes: [Okonomiyaki · a one-person gluten-free okonomiyaki bar on Dotonbori] A small, wildly decorated okonomiyaki bar at the western end of Dotonbori, run single-handed by its owner-chef, Shiho, and one of the most-collected gluten-free spots in Osaka on FMGF (59 public collections). Order at the counter from a clearly marked menu, find a table upstairs (some have a view), clear it yourself, and listen for your number. Drinks are self-service for ¥100 a go. There are about five gluten-free okonomiyaki (beef and onion, triple meat, mushroom and sausage), or build your own with vegetables and beans. Portions are huge, so a medium is plenty. The GF gyoza and fries are favourites. Queue before the roughly 6 pm opening. One woman does everything, so waits of 40 minutes or more are normal. One symptomatic celiac reacted in 2026, so it is not risk-free.

One diner credits the concept to a charismatic figure from the Shinshu (Nagano) ramen scene. Regulars come after drinking, and queues form late. Expect ¥2,000–3,000 a head. Cash only. It changed its name before March 2025.

The base is a standard Kyushu tonkotsu with very thin Hakata-style noodles. There's also a Kyushu-style abura-soba and hot, juicy gyoza. Smoking is allowed, and cards are not.

Opinions split: cheap, plentiful and "greatest meal my coeliac daughter has had since being in Japan" (July 2026), but others wanted more seasoning or preferred the okonomiyaki branch. Not a dedicated GF facility.

There is room for only one or two groups, so it's not for big parties.

osaka_kotan_namba_walk.notes: [Ramen · Osaka's old-school Kotan under Namba] A bright, 33-seat Kotan in the Namba Walk underground mall, steps from the Midōsuji Line, and for many Osakans the taste of childhood. The Kotan ramen comes in shoyu (soy-forward but not heavy) or shio (a light yet rich white broth), with thin noodles, chashu, bean sprouts, carrot and green onion. Regulars shower it in sesame from the table. The pork-belly Kotan is ¥950, a seasoned egg adds ¥120, and the spicy cold noodles with kimchi are ¥980 (September 2026). There are wonton noodles, and lunch sets with fried rice, gyoza or a croquette. Food comes fast, often in two minutes. A brisk hall manager in thick Osaka dialect keeps it moving.

osaka_kappa_ramen_honpo_sennichimae.notes: [Ramen · Kappa's 24-hour back-fat shoyu tonkotsu on Sennichimae] The main shop of Kappa Ramen Honpo, a 27-seat counter on Sennichimae-dōri, open around the clock. A standard Kappa ramen is ¥930, and kimchi and fried garlic are free, as are extra noodles from 6 am to 6 pm. Regulars add the kara-age and rice (¥350). September 2026 brought a limited, squid-ink-black tsukimi ramen (¥1,100). Order on the touch-panel machines inside the hard-to-spot entrance. One regular found the koi-me too strong at this branch.

osaka_menya_gaten_namba_shinsaibashi.notes: [Ramen · Jirō-style mazesoba in Amerikamura] The 15-seat head shop of Menya Gaten, since 2013, built on a Jirō-style "MAZE soba": thick, chewy, firm noodles (150 g up to 300 g) under vegetables, thick-cut chashu, fat and garlic, all scaled when you hand over your ticket. Mix it hard (one diner flipped it, "tenchi gaeshi"), and add mayo halfway. There's a curry mazesoba with a decent kick, and a DX chicken paitan ramen (¥1,400, August 2026) with tender thick chashu that won over a paitan fan. Kimchi and egg soup are free and self-serve, when they haven't run out. Some find the mazesoba merely salty without Jirō-style depth. Cash only, smoking allowed.

osaka_kinryu_ramen_honten.notes: [Ramen · the original Kinryu at the east end of Dotonbori] The main shop of the Kinryu dragon-sign chain, a 38-place counter with standing space at the Sakaisuji end of Dotonbori, open 24 hours. The bowl is Osaka's light tonkotsu, much lighter than Kyushu-style and easy to finish, with generous chashu. Even the plain ramen carries several slices and trimmings, and the chashu ramen piles it on. The ritual is unchanged for half a century, as one diner put it: free kimchi, garlic and garlic chives to load in as you like, plus free rice in place of extra noodles. Waits run 10–30 minutes at busy times. Buy a ticket first. Cash only, smoking allowed.

chef_bio.background: Main shop of Kinryu Ramen; a September 2026 reviewer says the free garlic, chives and kimchi have "remained unchanged for half a century".
chef_bio.specialty: Light Osaka tonkotsu with free kimchi and garlic.

osaka_ebi_shin_amemura.notes: [Ramen · lobster ramen in Amerikamura] A lobster-broth ramen and tsukemen shop in Amemura, since 2023, with a Japanese and English menu and plenty of overseas diners. The broth is rich and creamy with concentrated lobster, which one diner likened to a tonkotsu, over thick, chewy, curly noodles with plenty of vegetables and burdock chips. Pick a spice level from 0 to 4. Basic bowls started around ¥1,000–1,100 in 2025, and the showpiece adds a whole lobster for ¥4,200. osaka_tenchijin_sennichimae.notes: [Ramen · late-night tonkotsu on Aioibashi-suji] A 10-seat counter on the Aioibashi-suji shopping street, part of the Fukuchan group, open from lunch to 4 am and often run by a single cook. The standard is a straightforward tonkotsu ("moto-aji"). The ajitama ramen adds a slick of dark black garlic oil that gives the broth depth. For something lighter, the meat soba (¥880, July 2026) has a clear, refreshing broth with thin straight noodles, pork bits, onion and grated daikon. The abura-soba comes with three big slices of chashu, nori, and chili oil and vinegar at hand. There's also a spicy miso and a well-liked pork rice bowl. Buy a ticket out front.

osaka_kasu_udon_unotake.notes: [Udon · late-night kasu udon in Amerikamura] An 8-seat counter up a graffiti-covered corridor in Mitsudera Kaikan, the pink-lit building that is one of Amemura's deep-drinking landmarks. It serves Osaka's kasu udon: a clear, refreshing dashi enriched by crispy, fragrant abura-kasu (fried beef offal) and green onion, with firm udon. A spicy seasoning deepens as it melts in. Try the plum and tororo-kombu version. A regular of more than ten years says prices have risen to around ¥1,000, but the taste hasn't changed. It's a classic finish to a night out. The owner plays 80s and 90s hard rock (Guns N' Roses, Van Halen), and young crowds fill it by 10 pm. Closed Wednesdays. It plans to move by June 2027.

osaka_mithila_dotonbori.notes: [Indian · a 1999 Indian restaurant above Dotonbori] A long-running, 45-seat Indian restaurant up a flight of stairs on Dotonbori, its sign hidden among the neon near the Glico man. Choose spice 1–5, since the standard level is very mild. Tabelog flags vegetarian options. Smoking allowed.

Celiac travellers praise the gluten-free pizza, bolognese pasta, bread, açaí bowls and desserts. Expect a dose of wellness messaging (hot water, brown-rice enzyme samples). Open days follow a calendar, so book through LINE, and one diner wrestled with the online ordering.

osaka_republic_base_island_kitchen_kitah.notes: [Jamaican · gluten-free Jamaican cooking in Kitahorie] A tiny, cheerful Jamaican kitchen in Kitahorie. Celiac reviewers say it is 100% gluten-free, with a dedicated fryer, and it is also dairy-free with lots of vegan dishes. The owner cooks everything in view and is careful about gluten, even flagging that the beer isn't safe. Order the jerk chicken plate with crisp potato wedges (smoky, slightly spicy, well cooked), a jerk chicken bean wrap, tapas, or the popular nachos, which sell out after lunch. Save room for the cakes. Portions are big. Hours are unpredictable: 12–6 pm is typical, but several have arrived to find it shut, so check Facebook or Instagram first.

The ramen is a clear, gentle chicken-bone shio, made by pouring a yellow tare into the bowl, then the sparkling broth, with sesame, bean sprouts, green onion and thin straight noodles. One regular has visited more than 140 times. It was long run by a married couple; the owner now trains a younger team. Evenings only, closed Sundays, cash only.

osaka_kinryu_ramen_ebisubashi.notes: [Ramen · Kinryu off Ebisubashi-suji, with free rice] The Ebisubashi branch of the dragon-sign chain, just off the shopping street. The tatami-covered chairs are a Kinryu signature. Some find the rice soft. Cash only.

osaka_kotei_men_daichan_shinsaibashi.notes: [Ramen · a back-alley shio counter in Shinsaibashi, to 6 am] A long-running counter shop down an alley in Shinsaibashi's drinking district (one diner returned after 20 years), open from 6 pm until 6 am or sell-out. The order is the shio ramen: a light, clear chicken-bone broth with a gentle salt tare, slightly curly medium-thick noodles, mizuna and green onion. Melted butter or a seasoned egg rounds it out. The chashu don is sweet like eel sauce, a nice contrast, and the gyoza are sweet with cabbage. Opinions vary: some find it plain, and one reviewer thought the shoyu lacked character despite the media stickers. There is also a Daichan in Namba. Smoking allowed. Cash may be needed.

anecdotes.text: "The broth seems to be made from chicken bones, combined with a gentle salt tare, resulting in a light and clear soup. The noodles are slightly curly and medium-thick… Adding the melted butter enhances the richness." — April 2026, first visit in about 20 years.
"The 'Chashu Don' is richly flavored with a sweetness and depth reminiscent of eel sauce. The contrast with the light Sio Ramen is intriguing." — October 2025.

osaka_kamukura_ebisubashi.notes: [Ramen · a big Kamukura by NGK] A 67-seat Kamukura on a corner of the Namba shopping street near NGK, since 2024, run on touch panels and an automatic payment machine. osaka_chocolatta_karahori.notes: [Sweets · a gluten-free gâteau-chocolat café in Karahori] A small café in the retro Karahori district that began as a gluten-free gâteau-chocolat specialist. Its chocolate cake is made with naturally grown domestic rice flour, cane sugar, fermented butter and organic French and sustainable Belgian chocolate. It now also serves a gluten-free breakfast-and-lunch menu that celiac visitors rave about: French toast ("absolutely incredible"), waffles, a BLAT with egg, bacon and sausage plates, chicken sandwiches to take away. It is run by one person, so food can take a while, and it is pricey (about ¥5,000 for two plates and two coffees, October 2026). Only a few tables.

Reviewers love the zesty #1 ramen, the black garlic ramen and a rich miso, all with very tender pork, plus GF gyoza, GF beer and desserts, and a sake tasting. A vegan zesty ramen is also available. Sit at the counter for the show, or book the private room for a group. It is not a dedicated GF kitchen, but the staff are exceptionally knowledgeable.

osaka_ramen_ajidono_sennichimae.notes: [Ramen · Kansai-tuned iekei on Sennichimae-dōri] A 9-seat counter on Sennichimae-dōri, since 2011, serving a Yokohama iekei deliberately bent toward Osaka tastes. It comes with sturdy black nori and spinach, and a kick from the doubanjiang, garlic, sesame and vinegar on the counter. The ramen was ¥950 and the ajitama ramen ¥1,000 in 2026. Some say the broth and noodle portions run small. Weekdays it opens only for dinner, but it runs until 5 am. Buy a ticket at the small machine outside.

osaka_shinshin_seimen_higashishinsaibash.notes: [Ramen · late-night tantanmen in a Higashi-Shinsaibashi bar room] A dim, bar-like 12-seat room on the 3rd floor of a building with no street sign, open 8 pm to 6 am. It specialises in tantanmen. The dry version, the original style, coats the noodles in a nutty sesame sauce with chili oil and numbing Sichuan pepper (¥1,100, 2025); adjust it with sansho and niboshi vinegar. The soy-milk soup version is creamy and gentle, with chili oil optional, for those who don't like heat. On the side: "gyo-bao", grilled dumplings that burst like xiaolongbao (4 for ¥700), and a meat-miso mayo rice bowl (¥450). There's also a chuka soba whose broth one diner finished, and a popular "Guilty Jirō". Order on your phone at the seat. Open 9 pm to 6 am; smoking allowed.

osaka_tabucchan_sennichimae.notes: [Ramen · Sichuan tantanmen on the Nippombashi side] A 13-seat tantanmen shop with a few outdoor seats, dinner only, with queues that move fast. It cost ¥1,150 with cheese. Tame it with a raw egg or cheese, or go all in with extra cilantro. The yatai-style shoyu ramen also carries Sichuan pepper, over thin noodles. Portions are big, so come before you are too full. Cash only, smoking allowed.

osaka_sapporo_ramen_shishio_shinsaibashi.notes: [Ramen · Sapporo miso through the night in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A 14-seat counter serving Sapporo-style miso ramen from 6 pm until morning, and on Friday and Saturday nights until 2 pm the next day. The spicy version isn't very spicy. Buy a ticket at the door. It gets crowded late, but turnover is quick.

osaka_zundoya_shinsaibashi.notes: [Ramen · Zundoya's 24-hour Shinsaibashi branch] A 32-seat, round-the-clock Zundoya at the northern end of Shinsaibashi, with a few terrace seats. Lunch, 11 to 4, is set meals only, for example vegetable ramen with a small fried rice for ¥1,400 in October 2026. Buy a ticket at the entrance. Friendly, energetic staff.

Two-step ticket machine (QR, then pay); cash only.
osaka_naniwa_menjiro_kintetsu_namba.notes: [Ramen · a Tabelog Ramen 100 counter inside Kintetsu Namba station] A 12-seat counter inside the Kintetsu Osaka-Namba ticket gates, named to the Tabelog Ramen OSAKA "100" for 2025. Two clear, beautiful bowls: a free-range-chicken shoyu, oily but not heavy, deep with chicken and a clean finish, and a golden clam-broth ramen. Both come with rare chashu and pork-belly chashu, thick menma, mitsuba, yuzu and caramelised onion. A soft ajitama ramen with grilled chashu rice was ¥1,690 in October 2026, and the plain bowl has crept up to ¥1,150. Food arrives in three to five minutes. The ticket machine is a confusing two-step process (choose, get a QR code, scan and pay cash). If you're not travelling, a ¥180 station admission ticket is refunded as a discount.

chef_bio.background: Selected for Tabelog Ramen OSAKA "Tabelog 100" 2025 (Tabelog); a reviewer mentions an Umeda branch.

anecdotes.text: "The broth was rich in oil but not overly strong in flavor, allowing the delicious taste of the chicken to shine through. The toppings included rare chashu, pork belly chashu, a flavored egg, two thick pieces of menma, mitsuba, and yuzu." — October 2026, set ¥1,690, cash only.
"The soy sauce broth is rich with the flavor of free-range chicken, providing a deep taste while leaving a refreshing aftertaste." — October 2026.

osaka_asahi_seimen_namba_ramen_ichiza.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–21:30 (Tabelog). On the "Namba Ramen Ichiza" ramen floor (9F) of EDION Namba. Cash only; smoking allowed per Tabelog. High chairs available (October 2026).
osaka_asahi_seimen_namba_ramen_ichiza.notes: [Ramen · soy-tonkotsu chuka soba on EDION Namba's ramen floor] One of the shops on "Namba Ramen Ichiza", the 9th-floor ramen street in EDION Namba, and a regular's favourite there. The broth is a soy-sauce tonkotsu, comforting and fragrant, light yet deep for some and surprisingly rich and fatty for others. The shoyu ramen (¥980, June 2026) comes with thin curly noodles, and a fried-rice set adds ¥400. A spicy ramen with ajitama (¥1,150) has a real kick with garlic chives. There's also a curry ramen with big pieces of meat, and a minced-meat ramen with a small rice to mop up. The walls are signed by Yoshimoto comedians. Families come after toy shopping on 7F, and there are high chairs. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Shop on the Namba Ramen Ichiza floor of EDION Namba (ramen-ichiza.edion.com).

anecdotes.text: "I had the Shoyu Ramen for JPY 980 and the Fried Rice Set for JPY 400. The broth was light yet flavorful, with a nice depth from the soy sauce, and the thin, curly noodles had a delightful texture." — June 2026.
"The soy sauce-based tonkotsu broth is incredibly delicious and comforting… I'm convinced that Chuka Soba Asahi Seimen is still my favorite." — September 2026.

osaka_kotan_the_kitchen_namba_walk.vegan_detail: Not vegan: chashu, meat broth; set meals with meat.
osaka_kotan_the_kitchen_namba_walk.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–22:00 (L.O. 21:30); closed when Namba Walk is closed (Tabelog). Cards and e-money accepted.
osaka_kotan_the_kitchen_namba_walk.notes: [Ramen · Kotan's ramen-and-set-meal kitchen under Nippombashi] A newer format from Kotan, the Osaka ramen chain going since 1968: a bright counter-and-table kitchen in Namba Walk by the Nippombashi plaza, mixing the familiar KOTAN ramen with set meals. The shoyu or miso KOTAN ramen (miso ¥820, July 2026) comes with simple, satisfying chashu. Pair it with a mini fried rice or a tenshinhan set, which is unlike the usual Chinese-restaurant version. Gyoza (set ¥500), a chashu-egg set meal with miso soup and pickles, and a stir-fried meat-and-vegetable set suit rice people. In summer there's a bright-red spicy cold ramen with kimchi and smoked egg. One regular has been more than 30 times.

chef_bio.background: A new format from KOTAN Ramen (ramen-kotan.co.jp), "established in 1968" per an August 2026 review.

anecdotes.text: "I ordered the KOTAN Ramen Miso (JPY 820), along with the Gyoza Set Meal (JPY 500) and a Lemon Sour (JPY 380)… KOTAN Ramen has been the ramen I've eaten the most throughout my life." — July 2026.

"This is a new style of restaurant from KOTAN Ramen, established in 1968… The bright red soup in a flat bowl… pork belly chashu, smoked boiled egg, napa cabbage kimchi." — August 2026, spicy cold noodles.

osaka_shisen_ramen_soemoncho.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: house-made wheat noodles; soy-sauce broths.
osaka_shisen_ramen_soemoncho.hours_raw: Tabelog: Mon 0:00–7:00; Tue 21:00–24:00; Wed–Fri 0:00–7:00 and 21:00–24:00; Sat–Sun 0:00–9:00 and 21:00–24:00 — in practice a 9 pm-to-morning shop, closed Monday night. A reviewer found it opening late and out of Sichuan ramen one night (October 2026). Cash only (Tabelog).
osaka_shisen_ramen_soemoncho.notes: [Ramen · late-night Sichuan ramen in a Sōemonchō alley] Opened in December 2025 in a back alley off Sōemon-dōri: a 13-seat, two-floor shop that runs from 9 pm into the morning and is made for a post-drinks bowl. The signature Sichuan ramen (¥1,000) has a pleasantly spicy, rich broth over house-made thin noodles, almost somen-like, under a big heap of crunchy greens. Season it with garlic and lemon. A black shoyu ramen and a strong soy-sauce shoyu are the alternatives, and the fried rice (kimchi, or garlic and pepper) is good. Hours can slip: one October visitor arrived to find it opening late and out of Sichuan ramen. The stiff door is a known quirk. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: No source names the operator.

anecdotes.text: "I ordered the signature Sichuan ramen and kimchi fried rice. The rich and spicy broth paired perfectly with the homemade thin noodles, and I quickly finished it after adding garlic and lemon juice." — October 2026.
"I ordered the Sichuan Ramen for JPY 1000. It came with a generous amount of crunchy greens… the noodles were thin, similar to somen." — September 2026.
